newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends steady, gilts down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends steady, gilts down in dull trade.

text.p: Indian call money rates ended Monday at 0.50-0.75 percent little changed from opening quotes of 0.25-0.75, dealers said.
"There was no movement at all today, the rates started at 0.65 percent and closed at 0.50 percent,: a dealer at a state-run bank said.
"Rates moved up slightly towards close. Food-credit seems to be picking up and there was an outflow of approximately 2.0 billion rupees today," he said.
A forthcoming bond issue could put some pressure on call money rates, the dealer said.
State government bonds for 25 billion rupees are auctioned on April 30 and dealers expect good repsonse to the issue.
"Call money may firm up on outflows towards the loans but may not rise above 2.0 percent," the dealer said.
The state loan auction scheduled for April 30 is pushing seucirty prices down slightly, R.G. Bhat, a dealer at Mata securities said.
"The market expects the issue to be oversubscribed and the central bank to retain excess bids," he said.
Trade in governemnt securities was dull and prices fell for all maturities, dealers said.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange fell to 1.56 billion rupees from 1.88 billion at the weekend, dealers said.
The 13.80 percent government stock 2002 was traded on Monday at 107.00 rupees, 2.50 rupees down from the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) sale price. It traded on Saturday at 107.25 rupees.
The 13.65 percent 1999 stock was quoted at 105.90 compared to its RBI sale price of 107.09 rupees.
Certificates of deposit maturing in June 1997 yielded 6.50 percent, dealers said.
